# Artificial Intelligence: checkpoint

Twelve mixed GATE-style questions on the whole section, easy to hard. Chapters: [search](search.md) · [logic and inference](logic-and-inference.md) · [probabilistic reasoning](probabilistic-reasoning.md).

**Q1 (NAT, search).** Binary tree search, $b=2$, shallowest goal at depth $d=4$. Nodes generated by BFS up to depth 4 (including the root)?

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**Answer:** 31. **Solution:** $1+2+4+8+16=31$.

</details>

**Q2 (MCQ, search).** Which statement about A\* is **false**? (a) A consistent heuristic is admissible. (b) With $h=0$, A\* equals uniform-cost search. (c) An admissible heuristic guarantees optimal A\* **graph** search without re-opening nodes. (d) $h(\text{goal})$ must be 0 for an admissible heuristic.

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**Answer:** (c). **Solution:** graph search without re-opening needs **consistency**. (d): $h^*(\text{goal})=0$ so admissibility forces $h(\text{goal})=0$.

</details>

**Q3 (NAT, search trace).** Graph: $S\to A$ (1), $S\to B$ (4), $A\to B$ (2), $A\to C$ (5), $B\to C$ (1), $B\to D$ (5), $C\to G$ (3), $D\to G$ (2); children in alphabetical order. BFS (graph search, goal test on expansion) expands how many nodes including the goal?

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**Answer:** 6. **Solution:** queue order: $S,A,B,C,D,G$; $G$ is the sixth node popped.

</details>

**Q4 (NAT, search).** Same graph with $h(S)=6,h(A)=5,h(B)=3,h(C)=3,h(D)=2,h(G)=0$. Cost of the path found by greedy best-first minus the optimal cost?

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**Answer:** 4. **Solution:** greedy expands $S,B,D,G$: path $S\to B\to D\to G=4+5+2=11$; optimal $S\to A\to B\to C\to G=1+2+1+3=7$. $11-7=4$.

</details>

**Q5 (NAT, adversarial).** Game tree: root MAX, MIN, MAX, then 8 leaves left to right $2,4,6,3,1,7,5,0$. Minimax root value and the number of leaves **pruned** by left-to-right alpha-beta (give the sum)?

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**Answer:** 6. **Solution:** MAX layer: $4,6,7,5$; MIN layer: $\min(4,6)=4$, $\min(7,5)=5$; root $=5$. Alpha-beta: left MIN gets $\beta=4$ from the first MAX; in the second MAX, leaf $6$ gives $\alpha=6\ge4$ so leaf $3$ is pruned. Right MIN $(\alpha=4)$: first MAX gives 7; second MAX evaluates $5$ (value 5, $\alpha$ becomes 5, no cut since $\beta=7$) and $0$. Only 1 leaf is pruned. Sum $=5+1=6$.

</details>

**Q6 (NAT, propositional).** How many of the 8 models over $P,Q,R$ satisfy $(P\vee Q)\to R$?

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**Answer:** 5. **Solution:** false only if $P\vee Q$ is true (3 assignments) and $R=0$: 3 models; $8-3=5$.

</details>

**Q7 (MCQ, resolution).** From $(\neg P\vee Q)$, $(\neg Q\vee R)$, $P$, and the negated goal $\neg R$, which derivation reaches $\square$? (a) resolve first two to get $\neg P\vee R$, then with $P$ gives $R$, then with $\neg R$ gives $\square$ (b) the set is satisfiable (c) resolve $P$ with $\neg R$ (d) none.

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**Answer:** (a). **Solution:** $\neg P\vee Q$ and $\neg Q\vee R$ give $\neg P\vee R$; with $P$ gives $R$; with $\neg R$ gives $\square$. (c) shares no complementary pair.

</details>

**Q8 (MCQ, unification).** MGU of $P(x,\,f(y),\,z)$ and $P(a,\,f(z),\,b)$: (a) $\{x/a,\ z/b,\ y/b\}$ (b) $\{x/a,\ y/z\}$ (c) fails (d) $\{x/a,\ y/b\}$ only.

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**Answer:** (a). **Solution:** $x/a$; $f(y)$ vs $f(z)$: $y/z$; $z$ vs $b$: $z/b$. Apply to $y$: $y/b$. Combined: $\{x/a,z/b,y/b\}$.

</details>

**Q9 (MCQ, FOL).** Which formalises "some student likes every teacher"? (a) $\exists x\,(\text{S}(x)\wedge\forall y\,(\text{T}(y)\to\text{L}(x,y)))$ (b) $\forall x\,(\text{S}(x)\to\exists y\,(\text{T}(y)\wedge\text{L}(x,y)))$ (c) $\exists x\forall y\,(\text{S}(x)\to\text{L}(x,y))$ (d) $\exists x\,(\text{S}(x)\to\forall y\,\text{L}(x,y))$.

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**Answer:** (a). **Solution:** $\exists$ takes $\wedge$, $\forall$ takes $\to$. (b) is "every student likes some teacher".

</details>

**Q10 (NAT, Bayesian network).** Chain $X\to Y\to Z$, all binary: $P(X{=}1)=0.3$; $P(Y{=}1\mid X{=}1)=0.8$, $P(Y{=}1\mid X{=}0)=0.1$; $P(Z{=}1\mid Y{=}1)=0.9$, $P(Z{=}1\mid Y{=}0)=0.2$. Find $P(Z{=}1)$.

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**Answer:** 0.417. **Solution:** eliminate $X$: $P(Y{=}1)=0.3(0.8)+0.7(0.1)=0.31$. Eliminate $Y$: $P(Z{=}1)=0.31(0.9)+0.69(0.2)=0.279+0.138=0.417$.

</details>

**Q11 (MSQ, d-separation and parameters).** Network: $A\to C\leftarrow B$, $C\to D$ (all binary). Which are true? (a) $A\perp B$ (b) $A\perp B\mid D$ (c) $A\perp D\mid C$ (d) the network has 8 free parameters.

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**Answer:** (a), (c), (d). **Solution:** (a) collider unobserved. (b) false: $D$ is a descendant of the collider $C$, so conditioning on it makes $A,B$ dependent. (c) chain $A\to C\to D$ blocked by $C$ (and $B$-path: $A\to C\leftarrow B$ then to $D$ must pass $C$). (d) $1+1+4+2=8$.

</details>

**Q12 (NAT, naive Bayes as BN).** A naive Bayes classifier with a binary class and 10 binary features: how many free parameters, and how many for the full joint over the 11 variables? Give the difference.

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**Answer:** 2026. **Solution:** naive Bayes $=1+2\cdot10=21$; full joint $=2^{11}-1=2047$; difference $2047-21=2026$.

</details>
